A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoNight and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices. Corresponding experiments and displays can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA, day–night retrieval and depth-estimation evaluations, including appendix results and a prompting ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains those evaluations and adds original fine-tuning, transfer, annotation-consistency and evaluator-validation results.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 adds supervised adaptation of Qwen2.5-VL-7B through full-model, vision-encoder-only and LLM-only fine-tuning. This introduces a training procedure, while the benchmark construction and three-stage GPT-4.1 annotation pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use EgoNight-Synthetic, EgoNight-Sofia and EgoNight-Oxford, retaining 3,658 QA pairs, twelve QA categories, correspondence retrieval and depth estimation. The new adaptation and validation studies reuse existing coverage; their splits and sampling change experimental design rather than datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original VQA, retrieval and depth comparator sets remain unchanged. New Tables 2–3 compare base Qwen2.5-VL-7B with full, encoder-only and LLM-only fine-tuned variants, adding a limited set of adaptation comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 70/30 video-disjoint training/test design, synthetic-only training with unseen real-world evaluation, and parameter-freezing controls. New validation protocols involve four additional annotators on QA samples from twenty videos and human assessment of 300 judge-scored QA pairs. Existing benchmark sampling rates and retrieval/depth protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test synthetic-to-real transfer, cross-dataset performance correlation, which model components benefit from adaptation, and perception versus reasoning gains. Appendices add annotation-consistency and judge-bias/reliability checks, caption-generation examples and failure analysis. The difficulty-level averages summarize existing Table 1 results, rather than establishing a new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly reports Pearson correlation tests with p-values of 6.847 × 10^-5 and 1.462 × 10^-3. Appendices also quantify annotation similarity and judge agreement. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or random-seed counts.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark tables retain their numerical values. New results include synthetic-only transfer accuracy of 14.83% to 20.57%, and full fine-tuning improvements from 23.23% to 36.25% on synthetic and 16.40% to 25.61% on real held-out data. Appendices add 0.8458 annotation similarity and 95.67% judge–human agreement. Figure 12 corrects spatial answers to six/ten steps, while Figure 10 replaces a counting example with furniture identification under the counting label.

T1.justification: The retrieval-similarity, temporal-IoU and localization equations are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced; the added analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims that synthetic performance correlates with real-world performance, synthetic supervision transfers, and fine-tuning improves nighttime adaptation. The central contribution remains the same nighttime egocentric benchmark suite; its abstract and conclusion retain their substantive claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning synthetic-data validity, visual adaptation versus language alignment, persistent reasoning difficulties, annotator consistency and potential GPT-judge bias. It also explains specific VQA failures through illumination, lost detail, restricted visual cues and blur. Existing scale and environmental-coverage limitations remain, with expanded research directions.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a release promise with a code/data repository address. New Appendix A.8.5 documents consent, anonymization, audio removal and the Oxford source license; these are newly disclosed practices, not demonstrated preprocessing changes. Existing hardware, sampling and prompt details remain, while key hyperparameters for the new fine-tuning experiments are absent.

R1.justification: References are refreshed and pruned, adding works such as V2-SAM, Exo2EgoSyn and BLIP-2 while removing several peripheral citations and scene-editing/generation examples. The principal positioning against daytime egocentric benchmarks and EgoCross remains intact. Citation-style and publication-metadata changes do not establish additional substantive differences.

P1.justification: Dataset-construction passages in Section 3.1 are rewritten, some task labels are shortened, and dedicated analysis, acknowledgments and ethics sections are added. The overall narrative organization and much of the existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference template, substantially changing typography, margins, headers and figure/table placement throughout. It adds two fine-tuning tables and caption-generation Figure 13, revises Figure 5 styling, and resizes or rearranges appendix displays. Most original figures and tables retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added annotation and judge checks address validation gaps in v1, while controlled adaptation comparisons strengthen practical evidence. The gain is limited by missing fine-tuning hyperparameters and inconsistent correlation reporting: matched overall scores in Tables 11–13 yield approximately 0.899/0.967, rather than the 0.9359/0.8588 reported in Section 4.3, weakening that particular synthetic-validity argument.
